questions.stem: Given the inequality chain R ≤ T ≤ X ≤ V ≥ Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: R = T. II: R < T.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain R < U < T ≥ Z > Q, decide which conclusions follow. I: R ≤ T. II: Z < Q.

questions.stem: Statements: All farmers are teachers. Some readers are farmers. Conclusions: I. Some readers are teachers. II. Some teachers are readers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: The existing C∩A members must lie in B, proving both conclusions.

questions.stem: Statements: No readers are coders. All singers are coders. Some singers are coders. Conclusions: I. No readers are singers. II. Some singers are not readers. Which conclusion follows?

questions.explanation: All C members belong to B, disjoint from A; some C are explicitly given.

questions.stem: Statements: Some workers are singers. Some singers are painters. Conclusions: I. Some workers are painters. II. All painters are workers. Which conclusion follows?

questions.explanation: The specified intersections do not force A and C to overlap or include one another.

questions.stem: Statements: Some painters are artists. All artists are runners. Conclusions: I. Some painters are runners. II. All painters are runners. Which conclusion follows?

questions.explanation: Some A–B members must be C; not all A need be C.

questions.stem: Statements: No dancers are poets. Some poets are drivers. Conclusions: I. Some drivers are not dancers. II. No drivers are dancers. Which conclusion follows?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: The B∩C members are outside A; other C members remain unrestricted.
